Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei And Sister Daniela Sold $561 Million In Stock During IPO

# Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Sold $280 Million In Shares As Part Of Record IPO

By Siladitya Ray,

Forbes Staff.

 Siladitya Ray is a New Delhi-based Forbes news team reporter.

Nov 24, 2026, 02:19am EST Nov 24, 2026, 07:57am EST

## Topline

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sold $280.4 million worth of the artificial intelligence giant’s shares as part of its record-breaking initial public offering last week, according to a regulatory filing made on Monday, while his sister and company co-founder Daniela Amodei also disclosed an identical stock sale.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei both disclosed share sales worth around $280 million each.

AFP via Getty Images

## Key Facts

In a Form 4 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday, Amodei disclosed he sold 3,378,378 Anthropic shares to the IPO’s underwriters at the IPO price of $83 apiece on Friday.

After the sale, the billionaire CEO reported directly holding 202.8 million shares and restricted stock units, along with 35.9 million shares held indirectly through trusts over which he exercises investment or voting control.

Amodei’s combined reported holdings are worth approximately $20.9 billion based on Monday’s closing share price of $87.64.

Anthropic separately withheld 345,011 of Amodei’s shares, worth around $28.6 million at the IPO price, on Thursday to cover tax obligations arising from the vesting of his restricted stock units.

In a separate filing, Daniela Amodei, who serves as Anthropic’s president and board chair, also disclosed the sale of 3,378,378 shares at the $83 IPO price.

According to Anthropic’s IPO prospectus, all seven of the company’s co-founders were set to sell an identical number of shares in the offering, worth a combined $1.96 billion.

## forbes valuation

According to our estimates, both Dario and Daniela Amodei are each worth $20.9 billion, down around $301 million from the end of last week. Anthropic’s shares ended Monday down at $87.64, around 10% below their closing price on Thursday—the company’s first day of trading on the Nasdaq. Despite this drop, Anthropic’s shares are still 5.6% above their IPO price.

## what to watch for

Anthropic’s IPO prospectus outlines lock-up agreements that restrict its seven co-founders from selling most of their remaining shares for up to a year after the public offering. Under the terms outlined in the prospectus, the founders can sell up to 29% of their covered holdings after the release of Anthropic’s first-quarter 2027 earnings or 180 days after the date of the prospectus, which ever comes first.

## key background

Amodei co-founded Anthropic in 2021 after leaving rival AI firm OpenAI, where he served as vice president of research, along with six other former employees of the company. The maker of the Claude AI platform raised $81.3 billion in its IPO last week, surpassing the record set by Elon Musk’s SpaceX earlier this year for the largest public offering in history. On Friday, Anthropic announced the closing of its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase an additional 147 million shares, bringing total proceeds to $93.5 billion. The Claude-maker also raised an additional $26 billion through a concurrent private placement involving seven major technology companies, including Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and AMD. Despite owning a small percentage of the company’s overall equity, the seven co-founders retain control with around 50% of shareholder voting power.
